review_output: {"summary":"The SQL catches stale results at the right points: claim, finish and the current-report reader all compare the stored order revision with the live one. No tenant leak was found in the reader joins. The main risks are throughput and liveness: every payment or order change updates one merchant-wide row inside Serializable transactions. The trigger also runs as the calling role, which may not be allowed to write the revoked table; this still needs checking. Lock ordering between report jobs (generation, then version, then report) and evidence paths needs a synchronized test. Several findings below are unconfirmed risks and are labelled as such.","findings":[{"area":"performance","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015140000_live_metric_order_source/migration.sql","severity":"MAJOR","confidence":0.8,"issue":"One merchant-wide row is updated for every row change, and inserts and deletes are never filtered","evidence":"The row-level AFTER trigger always increments the merchant's revision on INSERT and DELETE. That includes draft orders and payments whose billingPurpose is not buyer_order. Updating one row from Serializable transactions forces concurrent webhooks for the same merchant to wait for each other and may fail them with serialization error 40001. Bulk statements increment the same row N times.","impact":"Payment webhooks for one merchant are processed one at a time, with extra retries and dead row versions in the table.","recommended_fix":"Skip inserts and deletes that the reader ignores: drafts, rows with billingPurpose other than buyer_order, and rows with no sourceLiveId. Use a statement-level trigger with transition tables to increment once per merchant. Consider tracking the revision per merchant and live (vendorId, sourceLiveId).","required_test":"Run two concurrent Serializable webhook transactions for the same merchant and measure the 40001 rate and wait time. Check that inserting a draft order or a payment with a different billingPurpose leaves the revision unchanged."},{"area":"correctness/liveness","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015150000_live_metric_order_report_binding/migration.sql","severity":"MAJOR","confidence":0.65,"issue":"Busy merchants may never get a ready report","evidence":"finish marks the report stale whenever the revision changed after create. Any order or payment change for the merchant, for any live, changes it. A worker read can take up to 30 seconds.","impact":"For merchants with steady payment traffic, workers recompute in a loop and every finish returns 0.","recommended_fix":"Narrow the revision scope to the merchant and live. Alternatively, bound retries and expose a 'superseded' status, or record a revision watermark when the snapshot is taken.","required_test":"Run a steady stream of payments for another live while a worker runs, and check that the report still reaches ready."},{"area":"tenant isolation/privileges","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015140000_live_metric_order_source/migration.sql","severity":"MAJOR","confidence":0.45,"issue":"The trigger runs as the calling role on a table that is revoked and RLS-protected (unconfirmed)","evidence":"The trigger function is not SECURITY DEFINER. The table has RLS enabled with no policies, and all access is revoked from anon, authenticated and service_role. Any payment or order write by a role that does not own the table would fail on the trigger's INSERT or UPDATE.","impact":"If such a role writes payments, every payment webhook is blocked.","recommended_fix":"Confirm which database role writes payments. If it is not the table owner, use a minimal SECURITY DEFINER function that only increments the counter, owned by the table owner.","required_test":"Insert and update a PaymentTransaction under the production writer role."},{"area":"lock ordering","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015140000_live_metric_order_source/migration.sql","severity":"MINOR","confidence":0.4,"issue":"A hidden lock on the generation row could reverse the lock order (unconfirmed)","evidence":"Writing to CommerceOrder or PaymentTransaction implicitly locks the generation row. If any transaction that already holds a version lock also writes those tables, it locks version before generation, the reverse of report jobs (generation, then version). Payment transactions that touch several merchants are also not globally ordered.","impact":"Possible deadlocks.","recommended_fix":"Check every transaction that writes commerce tables. Document that they never lock version or report rows, and add a check that enforces it.","required_test":"Synchronized race test: a report job's claim against an evidence or checkout transaction, using advisory locks to force the interleaving."},{"area":"performance/lock","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015150000_live_metric_order_report_binding/migration.sql","severity":"MINOR","confidence":0.7,"issue":"FOR UPDATE on the generation row serializes all report jobs for a merchant","evidence":"create, claim and finish only need to block revision increments, but FOR UPDATE also blocks each other across lives.","impact":"Unnecessary contention between report jobs for different lives.","recommended_fix":"Use FOR SHARE, which still conflicts with the payment trigger's UPDATE.","required_test":"Run claims for two lives of the same merchant concurrently and confirm neither waits for the other."},{"area":"correctness","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015150000_live_metric_order_report_binding/migration.sql","severity":"MINOR","confidence":0.75,"issue":"The stale update in claim and finish overwrites final statuses","evidence":"The UPDATE that sets status='stale' filters only by id and scope, with no status condition. It turns failed attempt_limit reports into stale.","impact":"Loses the record of a final failure.","recommended_fix":"Add AND status IN ('queued','running','ready').","required_test":"Claim a report that failed with attempt_limit after a revision bump, and check it stays failed."},{"area":"missed invalidation","file":"src/lib/live-metric-report-reader.ts","severity":"MINOR","confidence":0.35,"issue":"Some inputs to the order reader are not covered by the order revision (unconfirmed)","evidence":"readMetricOrderPage also depends on FormSubmission verificationStatus and verifiedAt, Live.formId, RegistrationForm.vendorId and LiveMetricRegistration. The order-source trigger does not watch these tables.","impact":"A report could be marked ready using outdated attribution if those changes don't increase the version's sourceRevision.","recommended_fix":"Confirm that triggers on these tables increase the version's sourceRevision.","required_test":"Change each dependency after create and check that finish returns 0 or the report becomes stale."},{"area":"performance","file":"src/lib/live-metric-report-reader.ts","severity":"MINOR","confidence":0.6,"issue":"Order pagination runs the full multi-table join again for every page, filtering on JSON metadata","evidence":"The filter on p.metadata->>'sourceLiveId' has no index shown, and keyset pagination on o.id sits on top of a join across six tables.","impact":"Total work grows roughly with the square of the number of orders, which uses up the read budget.","recommended_fix":"Add an expression index on PaymentTransaction (vendorId, (metadata->>'sourceLiveId')) and an index on CommerceOrder (vendorId, id). Check the plan with EXPLAIN.","required_test":"Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on a merchant with a large number of orders."}]}
